Public Participation Information
  In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493,
  2498 and 2499, due to the continuing state of emergency, including masking and social distancing
  directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being held remotely via
  teleconference.  There will not be a physical location for this meeting. Members of the public may
  participate in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 815 0377 4455, Meeting Password: 784330. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 815 0377 4455, Meeting Password: 784330. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  MARCH 21, 2022

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 7:00 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
  Executive Order N-29-20.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Bain, McCormick, Pope, & Romanelli

  Commissioners Absent:  Ciarolla, Persichina, & Retz

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Daniel A-Haja

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION SPECIAL MEETING DRAFT MINUTES
  OF FEBRUARY 15, 2022

  VICE CHAIR BAIN noted a correction on page 5 clarifying a statement made by her
  that the private pickleball lesson she took did not take place at the South Bay Tennis
  Center; it was offered by a private instructor who held a small group class, and it is
  that instructor who offered to assist the City in setting up a pickleball program.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK to:

  APPROVE MINUTES AS REVISED.

  There being no objection, VICE CHAIR BAIN so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES  1
MARCH 21, 2022
   6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  **ITEM 6E. TAKEN OUT OF ORDER**

  E.  CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICES TURF REMOVAL PROGRAM

  Assistant City Manager (ACM) Davis provided some background information on the
  item and introduced Tammie Myers and Angie Gilbride of California Water Service
  (Cal Water).

  Tammie Myers of Cal Water presented information regarding the program and
  potential projects and locations.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN stated the program was also suggested to the Environmental
  Advisory Committee (EAC) and was well received by its members. She asked staff
  if the area at City Hall to the south is amenable to grass removal or if it is used for
  events. ACM Davis responded that City Hall is not used for events other than the
  outdoor patio area for outdoor meetings. VICE CHAIR BAIN inquired if Cal Water
  would assist in landscape design, or if funding is provided to the City to hire a
  landscaper. Tammie Myers responded that she is currently working with landscape
  contractors who design and estimate costs at such locations, and that budgets
  provided by the City are observed by the contractor. She added that the cost of the
  design would come out of the rebate offered to the City.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked about the rebate and if the City would need to pay
  the $93,000 up front and get reimbursed by Cal Water. Tammie Myers stated that
  she aligned this program to an existing turf removal program which combines a turf
  removal program and a spray-to-drip program. The numbers are calculated by
  square footage with $3/sq. ft. for turf removed and $3.50/sq. ft. for areas wherever
  overhead spray is replaced by a drip system. She stated that the potential rebate
  would be $93,000 which would offset the cost of design, install, and materials for
  the project. Angie Gilbride stated that it represents the maximum amount of turf that
  can be removed from that site and could be lowered with a corresponding dollar
  amount.

  Tammie Myers shared that she went to Highridge Park with Maintenance
  Superintendent Goldsmith and identified portions of the park that are watered but
  not utilized and could use turf replacement and a drip system. The area proposed
  for turf replacement is 41,000 square feet and would be eligible for up to $144,000
  in rebates. That project would be less design intensive and could be accomplished
  with the City’s current contractor. It would also show nearby residents an example
  of how to limit water use in their own homes.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked if the location behind the softball field would be
  included in the turf removal and if signage would be posted for residents that

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES  2
MARCH 21, 2022
   describes the plants and drip system used. Tammie Myers responded that the
  grass area directly behind the backstop would not be removed, and that the signage
  could be included in the project. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted
  signage could also be done as a Scout project.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN clarified that the signage, design, and square footage is
  determined by the City and could be a fun project. She asked if the rain basin would
  promote water savings below the ground. Tammie Myers responded that it is to
  promote a rain basin area to prevent puddling and allows water to go back into the
  ground, acting as a passive system. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith also
  pointed out an area of Highridge Park where water drains and suggested installing
  stones in the area to allow drainage. Tammie Myers added that the far side of the
  path would be used and that benches could be added to the area as well.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN asked if there were any prompts from other projects with similar
  square footage. Tammie Myers noted that there are no current projects like this but
  that she can pull information from other cities.

  ACM Davis noted the project was presented to the EAC and City Council, both of
  whom expressed interest in proceeding. The timing of the project would require the
  application to be submitted within a month for both projects with the work to be
  completed within four months. She stated that it was suggested to form a
  subcommittee which would include members from the Commission, EAC, and
  Council. This subcommittee would help with design and the scope of the projects.
  The next steps would be to go to Council with a budget adjustment in April and
  appoint a subcommittee. She asked if any Commissioners would be interested in
  joining the subcommittee.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN volunteered to join the subcommittee and was in favor of the
  projects. She shared her personal experience with a low water landscape. She
  knows planning is important for the project and that choosing the right landscaper
  should be something the subcommittee studies. She suggested asking the
  Commissioners not in attendance today as well as bringing the findings back to the
  EAC. She asked why the timeline was four months as it seemed short. Tammie
  Myers responded that the oncoming stage 2 drought presented an opportunity for
  larger projects like this one and that funding could only be held for a limited amount
  of time to ensure its use. VICE CHAIR BAIN asked if the project funding was a
  rebate and if the funding would be initially paid by the City and then reimbursed by
  the rebate. Tammie Myers responded that the application would be filled out by the
  City and would be inspected as the project is being completed; afterwards the City
  would be reimbursed. VICE CHAIR BAIN asked if the contractors wait for the rebate
  or if the City pays them up front. Tammie Myers noted some cities pull from their
  budget with Council approval and then get reimbursed. ACM Davis responded the
  City would use its own funds and be reimbursed like past projects.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES  3
MARCH 21, 2022
   No further action taken.

  A.  PARK AND RECREATION PROGRAM REVIEW

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a review of the staff report.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN commended staff for taking on an ambitious review.

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  B.  PROPOSED PARK TOUR SCHEDULE

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a review of the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked about the purpose of the visit to Peter Weber
  Equestrian Center and if it would be added to the yearly park tours. Community
  Services Supervisor Pinuelas responded that the visit would serve to tour the facility
  with owner Gil Houle and was suggested because of the recent contract renewal
  and the opportunity it presents to visit the facility and learn more about proposed
  improvements. She added that staff is not recommending the visit be added to the
  annual park tour schedule. The meeting was proposed to take place at 6 pm on
  September 19th before the regular Commission meeting.

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  C.  REQUEST FOR STREET TREE REMOVALS - LARGA VISTA

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith provided a review of the staff report.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN asked about the removal cost per tree and if street repair would
  be needed. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith responded that it would be
  $1,200 per tree and $190 for a replacement tree. He added that no replacement
  species had been decided yet and that no street repair would be needed though
  minor buckling in the road and cracks in the curb and gutter would be addressed at
  a later date.

  In response to COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK’s question, Maintenance
  Superintendent Goldsmith responded that they would be used as mulch on the
  outside of right-of-way’s due to the high leaf content.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI thanked the Maintenance Superintendent for
  bringing the matter to the Commission’s attention and asked why this was brought
  to the Commission given that the Commission relinquished the responsibility to
  make these types of decisions. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted that

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES  4
MARCH 21, 2022
   due to the number of trees being removed within proximity on the same street, staff
  decided the removal warranted informing the Commission.

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  D.  SUMMER MOVIE NIGHT AND CONCERT PROGRAM

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja gave a brief overview of the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER POPE had no preference for the movie selections.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK would like to “Sing 2” as a movie selection.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN suggested “Soul” be another movie selection.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI had no preference for the movie selections.

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja noted that “Sing 2” would be scheduled
  for June 11 and Soul for July 9.

  COMMISSIONER POPE shared that she is in favor of supporting the local PV
  Symphonic Band for the concert in the park as a local band in the community and
  would like to break up the movie nights by holding the concert in July. She also
  recommended seeking grant funding from Los Angeles County that was available
  in the past.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN expressed support for Option 2 of the presented report and
  wanted to know how the PV Symphonic Band was received last year. Community
  Services Coordinator A-Haja noted positive responses to last year’s event.
  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted that about 200-250 attended last year’s
  concert and that there was a Snow Cone truck. He asked if both a band and the
  Symphonic Band could be in attendance. ACM Davis noted the logistics and added
  costs may be an issue, but staff would follow Commission’s and City Council’s
  recommendation. COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK was in favor of Option 1 of the
  presented report; he shared that he enjoyed the PV Symphonic Band but expressed
  wanting to see how a different band could affect the event and attendance.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN asked how the Commission felt about breaking up the movie
  nights with a concert in July and if staff could find a youth act such as a local high
  school band to add to the concert. COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK recommended
  Peninsula High’s Jazz group as they were well-received at the Jack Kramer Club in
  a past event. VICE CHAIR BAIN asked if staff could investigate a youth warm up
  act for the event and bring findings back on a later date. She also asked for more
  information about food trucks. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas responded
  that two to three food trucks serving different food and drinks would be sourced.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES  5
MARCH 21, 2022
   VICE CHAIR BAIN noted the popularity of food trucks and requested an adequate
  number of tables and chairs be available for those in attendance.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if this event was included in the budget.
  ACM Davis noted it would be adopted in the budget for next fiscal year which starts
  in July. He shared that he was in favor of Option 2.

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja polled the Commissioners regarding their
  preference for the concert options presented and music genres. VICE CHAIR BAIN,
  COMMISSIONER POPE, and COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI chose Option 2.
  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK chose Option 1. Genres selected by the
  Commission ranged from Western, Americana, Patriotic, Country, and Jazz.
  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked what genres were available from bands in
  the community but was in favor of Jazz.

  ACM Davis stated that staff will return with more information based upon the
  guidance received.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if these items will be included in the next
  fiscal budget. ACM Davis affirmed that all proposed events will be proposed in next
  year’s budget.

  7.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  TENNIS COURT RESURFACING UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas noted resurfacing would take begin the
  week of April 11th and that the Tennis pro was made aware. She added that the
  resurfacing would take place in a phased approach and would take three to four
  weeks to complete.

  B.  MAYOR’S RIDE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas stated that staff started initial planning for
  the May 21st event. She shared that staff has secured horses for the event and will
  update the Commission as details are finalized.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted downed eucalyptus tree limbs about ¾ of
  the way up the George F Canyon trail. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith
  took note and stated staff will investigate the area. Maintenance Superintendent

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES  6
MARCH 21, 2022
   Goldsmith also noted a resident near the top of the lookout point had fenced in
  part of the trail and will work with the Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy
  to address the issue.
  VICE CHAIR BAIN noted the mural progress at Highridge Park and asked if the
  murals were finished. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas responded that
  the artist will finish the bulletin boards this week and staff plans to hold a ribbon
  cutting ceremony in April.
  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)
  NONE.
  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF FEBRUARY 22, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  BUTCHER PARK UPDATE

  ACM Davis noted the City has been in discussions with the Municipal Water District
  (MWD). She shared that MWD has moved its project date up and the City Council’s
  Subcommittee will meet with them and then the full City Council will discuss the
  issue in April. She shared that the plans would move forward and the City will have
  shovel-ready project plans. ACM Davis noted that she would likely be able to
  provide an update by May. She added that there may be rental cost for the land
  that will be used by the MWD, in response to VICE CHAIR BAIN.

  B.  CHANDLER PARK PLAYGROUND SURVEY

  ACM Davis noted the survey has been out for a month and that it would be pushed
  out again closer to the end of the month. She added that staff will bring the results
  to the Commission at the next meeting and noted there will also be a Chandler Park
  tour meeting in April.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN asked how many surveys had been returned so far. ACM Davis
  did not have exact numbers but mentioned that several stake holders had
  responded. She noted the survey was sent out to the schools, the Peter Weber
  Equestrian Center, equestrians, and nearby neighborhoods.

  C.  NATURE CENTER UPDATE

  ACM Davis noted staff will likely come to the Commission with update in April or it
  may be paired with the visit at George F Canyon. She stated that a 30% design
PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES  7
MARCH 21, 2022
   drawing is estimated to be completed by early April and that staff is seeking funding
  opportunities. She shared that staff has reached out to state representatives’ hoping
  discretionary money could be granted for funding and will also be applying for
  available federal grants. She shared that Commission suggestions are welcomed
  and that a Pepper Tree Foundation fundraising committee will be formed to help
  identify further funding opportunities.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked about Rockbluff Park play equipment. ACM
  Davis noted the equipment is delayed but the project will be completed this fiscal
  year. She shared that she was invited to join Rollingwood’s “Let’s Chat meeting” on
  Thursday and will be giving them an update. She added that she was awaiting more
  specifics and hoped to be able hold a ribbon cutting in June.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI reminded the Commission of the South Bay Cities
  Council of Government’s general meeting. ACM Davis noted City Manager
  Grammar will be in attendance.

  11.  ADJOURNMENT

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted he will be unable to attend April’s meeting.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN asked where April’s meeting would be held. ACM Davis noted
  the 6 pm meeting will take place in the City Council Chambers.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  ADJOURN THE MEETING AT 8:25 PM TO THE NEXT ADJOURNED PARK
  AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON APRIL 18, 2022, AT 6:00
  P.M., WHICH WILL BE HELD IN THE CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS, 4045
  PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH, ROLLING HILLS ESTATES.

  There being no objection, VICE CHAIR BAIN so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  ___________________________
  Daniel A-Haja  Judy Bain
  Community Services Coordinator  Vice Chair, Park & Activities
  Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES  8
MARCH 21, 2022
